name: Pure pawn ending — opposition and key squares

plans.label: Take the opposition
plans.description: Place the king so the kings face each other with one square between and the opponent to move: whoever must step aside concedes the path. From far away, take the distant opposition — an odd number of squares between the kings — and convert it step by step.

success.note: The kings form direct or distant opposition with Black to move.

plans.label: King ahead of the pawn on the sixth
plans.description: A pawn escorted from behind by its king is a spectator; one whose king owns the squares in front queens itself. Get the king to the sixth rank or beyond while the pawn is still no further than the fifth.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Occupy the key squares', whose success needed key squares defined relative to the pawn. It is now the relationship the key squares exist to create: White's king has reached the sixth rank or beyond while the pawn is still no further than the fifth, so the king is ahead of its own pawn. Which sixth-rank square it is on is not checked. Original success note: 'Key squares are defined relative to king positions the vocabulary cannot read.'

plans.label: Triangulate to lose a move
plans.description: When the straight approach is met head on, walk the king around a triangle the defending king cannot copy and return to the same position with the other side to move; corresponding squares decide who runs out of safe steps first.

success.note: Triangulation is a move-order fact; a static census cannot see who is to move.

plans.label: Hold the opposition
plans.description: Meet the attacking king head on and keep it off the key squares; give ground only straight backward along the pawn's file, never diagonally aside, and fall back onto the squares in front of the pawn.

success.note: Black holds the opposition, direct or distant: the kings stand on one line with an odd number of squares between them and it is White to move. The earlier note called this an outcome with no signature; the vocabulary has king_opposition, which is a first-class predicate for exactly this and which reads the side to move. It certifies the opposition at the moment measured, not that Black held it to the end.

plans.label: Shoulder and race
plans.description: When pure defence fails, count the race: use the king's body to shoulder the enemy king off its path while your own king runs at the pawns — the defender's king fights with its shoulders, not just its feet.

success.note: Race counting is calculation, not a position census.

watch: Fires for any kings-and-pawns-only position, from a bare-kings draw to a ten-pawn race; the entry names the family, not a verdict about this position.
The opposition plan is mechanically visible; key squares, triangulation, holding, and races still require their own evidence.
Colour convention: White is authored as the stronger/attacking side. Mirror the plans when the colours are reversed; the trigger fires only for the White-side census.
typicalMistakes: Pushing the pawn before the king owns its key squares — each premature push moves the key squares further away and can throw away the win in one move.
Taking the opposition mechanically when the position wants a key-square end-run around it.
Losing the race by stopping to capture pawns instead of shouldering and running.
Forgetting that a rook-pawn plus the wrong king position is a stock draw the opposition cannot fix.

sources: Family per design/04-content-architecture.md section 4 (pawn: opposition, key squares, triangulation, corresponding squares).

Tablebase honesty: minimal cases of this family (king and pawn versus king — three pieces) are trivially inside tablebase range and a tablebase CAN verify them; the family as triggered often exceeds seven pieces, where no tablebase exists. Nothing in this entry was tablebase-checked.
UNGROUNDED: plan, watch, and mistake prose is authored endgame-literature consensus rendered by the author; no engine or tablebase has graded any claim in this entry.

Trigger scope: the trigger is exactly 'no pieces but kings and pawns' and fires for trivial positions too. Direct and distant opposition are now mechanically visible; pawn-relative key squares and move-history claims remain outside the trigger.

Degenerate guard added 2026-08-15: the trigger is a pure 'no piece heavier than a pawn' census and therefore fired on the census instrument's `bare_kings` board, a position with no pawns in an entry about pawn opposition and key squares. A clause requiring at least one pawn somewhere on the board was added. Measured before and after: corpus firings 33 of 694 in both runs (9 pawn-breakthrough-convert, 24 pawn-opposition-convert); degenerate firings [bare_kings, king_and_one_white_pawn, king_and_one_black_pawn] -> [king_and_one_white_pawn, king_and_one_black_pawn], the two single-pawn boards being genuine members of this family.
